lines.trans: Dima, where is the second set of keys to the car?
Dima never throws words to the wind.
Vityusha, take the second key, the car is yours.
Oh you schemer, you stole your own car!

It is a pity, of course, that everything fell through today.

examples.text: Ладно, давай мы попозже поговорим.
examples.trans: Alright, let's talk a little later.

examples.text: Помнишь, как мы с тобой в окопах были?
examples.trans: Remember how you and I were in the trenches together?

examples.text: Ведь мы же с тобой одной крови.
examples.trans: After all, you and I are of the same blood.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Помнишь, как мы с тобой в окопах были?
examples.trans: Remember how you and I were in the trenches together?

examples.text: И про эту машину тоже не забывай.
examples.trans: And do not forget about this car either.

examples.text: И про машину не забывай.
examples.trans: And do not forget about the car.

meanings.en: to sit down, to take a seat
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'есть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sit down', paired with 'садиться'.

examples.text: Послушайте, сядьте, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Listen, sit down, please.

examples.text: Он сел на стул.
examples.trans: He sat down on a chair.

examples.text: Послушайте, сядьте. Сядьте, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Listen, sit down. Sit down, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'камейка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'bench' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Для начала мы бы сели на скамейку.
examples.trans: To start with, we would have sat down on a bench.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть скамейка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always bench.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лёва, я тебе потом всё объясню.
examples.trans: Lyova, I will explain everything to you later.

examples.text: Лёва, я потом всё объясню.
examples.trans: Lyova, I will explain everything later.

examples.text: Ты думаешь, что ты здесь, потому что великий повар?
examples.trans: Do you think you are here because you are a great chef?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'круг').

examples.text: Потом вокруг нас зажглись бы гирлянды.
examples.trans: Then fairy lights would have lit up around us.

examples.text: Она вокруг меня бегала.
examples.trans: She was running after me (around me).

examples.text: Посмотри вокруг.
examples.trans: Look around.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'жечься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lit up'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и зажечься вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and lit up on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют зажечься.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to lit up.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'fairy lights' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Потом вокруг нас зажглись бы гирлянды.
examples.trans: Then fairy lights would have lit up around us.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть гирлянда.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always fairy lights.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Димочка, ну не расстраивайся ты так.
examples.trans: Dimochka, well do not get so upset.

examples.text: У меня сейчас сплошные нервы и стресс.
examples.trans: I have nothing but nerves and stress right now.

examples.text: Я новый контракт не могу подписать.
examples.trans: I cannot sign a new contract.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to submit, file; to serve', paired with 'подавать'.

examples.text: Тут оценки за интерьер, подачу и блюдо шефа.
examples.trans: Here are ratings for interior, presentation, and the chef's dish.

examples.text: Зато подача у блюда очень креативная.
examples.trans: At least the presentation of the dish is very creative.

examples.text: Он подал инспектору свой фирменный паштет!
examples.trans: He served the inspector his signature pâté!

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.text: И нам подали бы горячий глинтвейн.
examples.trans: And they would have served us hot mulled wine.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea.

examples.text: Осторожно, чашка очень горячая.
examples.trans: Careful, the cup is very hot.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'mulled wine' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: И нам подали бы горячий глинтвейн.
examples.trans: And they would have served us hot mulled wine.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть глинтвейн.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always mulled wine.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'returned', paired with 'возвращать'.

examples.text: Вернут пропажу вечером у ботанического сада.
examples.trans: They will return the missing item this evening by the botanical garden.

examples.text: А потом тебе бы вернули пропажу.
examples.trans: And then they would have returned your missing hat.

examples.text: Тебе бы вернули пропажу.
examples.trans: They would have returned your missing item.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'пажа'). Common feminine noun meaning 'missing thing' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вернут пропажу вечером у ботанического сада.
examples.trans: They will return the missing item this evening by the botanical garden.

examples.text: А потом тебе бы вернули пропажу.
examples.trans: And then they would have returned your missing hat.

examples.text: Тебе бы вернули пропажу.
examples.trans: They would have returned your missing item.
